parsed.explanation: The combined operative regime layers a documented national exposure on top of comparatively protective state law. At the border every trans visitor passes through a binary-sex document regime: X markers stopped, passports blocked or confiscated with travellers stranded, and a refusal/fraud-ineligibility pathway for suspected discrepancies — an unavoidable, state-engineered discovery exposure with no documented operative remedy (litigation unresolved). Documented custody harms — removal of hormones, forced labour, beatings and sexual abuse — put detention at tier 1-2 severity. Within the division, anti-discrimination law, hate-crime enhancement, panic-defence abolition and a 2026 civil-rights finding give real, working recourse; but the state banned minors' gender-affirming care (affecting travelling minors and parents), and foreign governments issue travel advisories over this country's document rules. Net: materially above the division-free worst cases, but capped by unremedied universal entry exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: National binary-sex passport rule; X-marker processing halted; passports confiscated/blocked, travellers stranded; visa officers instructed to refuse where documents cast doubt on sex, with possible lifetime fraud ineligibility.
entry_documents.protection: Civil-liberties suit pending; limited waiver exists for fraud findings, but never shown applied.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry exposure feeds national record systems and downstream encounters; no documented pre-emption by state law.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau mandates haircut/removal of hormones/'conversion therapy' policies for trans inmates from 2026; immigration-custody trans men report forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, severe sexual abuse.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: None documented in custody; rescission of prison LGBTQ order.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any state arrest or immigration matter routes into national custody rules.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National orders bar congruent facility access in funded single-sex facilities; in many state/provinces, government-building bans; in 4, criminal exposure (trespass-style, refusal-to-depart trigger; documented arrest and 24h men's-ward holding).
federal_state_facilities.protection: In this division, no documented bathroom/facility ban; anti-discrimination law covers public accommodations.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: National facilities rules apply in national buildings regardless of division law.

care_services.exposure: Division bans gender-affirming care for minors (puberty blockers, HRT, surgery), removing access even where medically necessary; grandfather clause only. National subpoenas of hospitals for under-19 patient records raise outing/records exposure; national funding bans pending.
care_services.protection: Adult care not banned here; public-insurance surgery ban lifted 2017.
care_services.interaction: Travelling trans minors and parents cannot obtain or continue care; prescriptions for adults face ordinary checks only.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'neutralization' of 'radically pro-transgender' groups; December 2025 reward memorandum frames 'radical gender ideology'; 190+ anti-trans bills in 2023; known-arrest precedent in a sister jurisdiction.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Employment discrimination prohibited nationally (2020 ruling); division hate-crime enhancement and enforced civil-rights statute.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State framing does not neutralise national framing; both operate on one traveller.

minors_guardians.exposure: Care ban (with provider discipline and civil suits) applies to travelling minors; sports ban with birth-certificate gate (stayed); national EO directs prosecution of facilitators; parents carrying trans minors risk scrutiny of records.
minors_guardians.protection: Grandfather clause for existing treatment; 2024 state court ruling protecting trans students (privacy/autonomy).
minors_guardians.interaction: Minor-focused rules create a distinct, higher-risk profile for travelling families than for adults alone.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Division ranked second-highest raw anti-LGBTQ incident count in 2025 (no denominator); characterised as regionally least safe for trans people after 2025 changes.
street_violence_police_response.protection: July 2026 court finding against a man who struck a trans woman; hate-crime enhancements since 2019; panic defence abolished 2024; 88% poll support for protections.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Recourse documented as operating; census lacks per-capita weighting.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Sports-ban status unresolved; whether care bans enjoined unknown; incident census without denominators; national litigation on passports unresolved, so exposure depends on travel date.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Legal-aid FAQ and identity-document guidance exist; state anti-discrimination enforcement demonstrated in court.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Unresolved national litigation can tighten or relax the border layer mid-trip.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar national-layer universal exposure (birth-sex facility/document rules, unremedied), but this division adds working anti-discrimination enforcement, hate-crime recourse and no local facility ban — better than the anchor's wholly unremedied picture.

Close analogue: universal, unremedied state-ordered screening exposure plus partial local protections. Here the exposure is at the border (documents, fraud referrals) plus documented custody abuse, arguably more severe; the division layer is stronger than the anchor's thin mitigation, netting similar or slightly above.

The 0.55 anchors show recurring but partially remedied friction without universal rules; this jurisdiction's national border regime is a harder, universal, document-based exposure with no operative remedy, and custody abuse is documented — it must sit below 0.55.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters two regimes: a national layer that binarises documents, halts X markers, instructs refusal/fraud referral on suspected discrepancy, restricts facilities, and runs custody with documented hormone removal and sexual abuse — a tier-1/tier-2 universal exposure whose only documented remedy is pending litigation — and a division layer with genuinely working protections: enforced anti-discrimination law, a 2026 civil-rights judgment, hate-crime enhancement, and the abolished panic defence, but with minors' care banned and records subpoenaed nationally. Entry and any custody encounter expose the traveller regardless of division law; ordinary in-state daily life offers real recourse. The combination yields elevated risk: protective enough to avoid the 0.35 band, capped below 0.55 by the unremedied universal border and custody exposures.
